fields.description: the hero who gave the troops; the event only carries the hero side of the giving party

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the settlement that received the garrison

triggers.name: playerPartyStarving
triggers.description: The player's party is still without food another day — fires once per day from the second day of a starvation streak on, right after the daily starvation morale hit.

triggers.name: playerStartedTalkFromMenu
triggers.description: The player started a conversation with `hero` from the map or a location menu — hook for a companion to react when addressed directly or when the player talks to someone nearby.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero the player is about to talk to

triggers.name: playerJoinedTournament
triggers.description: The player entered the tournament in `town` from its menu; `isParticipant` is true when they compete themselves, false when they only start spectating — no bracket has run yet.

fields.name: town
fields.description: the town holding the tournament

fields.name: isParticipant
fields.description: true = the player signed up to compete; false = the player began watching

triggers.name: heroCreated
triggers.description: A brand-new hero entered the world somewhere — a wanderer appearing in a tavern, a newborn, a notable; it also fires for heroes other mods (and this one) spawn, so filter by who was created.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the newly created hero

fields.name: bornNaturally
fields.description: true only for naturally born newborns; false for wanderers and every factory-created hero

triggers.name: heroActivated
triggers.description: A hero woke up into the active world; `previousState` says where they came from — `Fugitive` marks a dismissed companion reappearing in a tavern.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who became active

fields.name: previousState
fields.description: the game's Hero.CharacterStates they were in before, e.g. Fugitive

triggers.name: heroOccupationChanged
triggers.description: A hero's occupation changed — the classic case is a companion granted a fief turning into a lord; the payload carries the old value, the new one is on the hero (`hero.occupation`).

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who changed occupation

fields.name: oldOccupation
fields.description: the game's Occupation before the change, e.g. Wanderer

triggers.name: heroLeveledUp
triggers.description: A hero gained a level, after the game handed out the focus points (and one attribute point every fourth level); fires for the player, companions and AI heroes alike.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who gained the level

triggers.name: heroGainedSkill
triggers.description: A hero's skill ticked up one or more whole skill levels — companion skill-up remarks.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero whose skill improved

fields.name: skill
fields.description: the game's skill id

fields.name: change
fields.description: how much the skill rose

triggers.name: heroJoinedParty
triggers.description: A hero joined a party on the map — a just-hired wanderer riding out to their lord, a notable joining a caravan or a garrison turning over; it fires everywhere, not only for the player.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who joined

fields.name: party
fields.description: the party they joined

triggers.name: companionAdded
triggers.description: The player hired a new companion — when this fires the hero is already in the player's clan and party, so greeting lines can reference them directly.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the new companion

triggers.name: playerMetHero
triggers.description: The player met a hero for the first time — a conversation happened or the encyclopedia revealed them; first-meeting chatter.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero the player met

triggers.name: playerTraitChanged
triggers.description: One of the player's personality traits crossed a level boundary (only at levels, never for trait XP alone); the five that move at runtime are Mercy, Honor, Valor, Generosity and Calculating.

fields.name: trait
fields.description: the game's trait id, e.g. Honor

fields.name: previousLevel
fields.description: the trait level before (a jump of two levels still fires once)

fields.name: newLevel
fields.description: the trait level now, read live from the player hero

triggers.name: perkUnlocked
triggers.description: A hero unlocked a perk — usually the player picking one at a level-up; AI heroes open perks too, so check who it was.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who opened the perk

fields.name: perk
fields.description: the game's perk id

triggers.name: relationChanged
triggers.description: The relation between two heroes moved by `change` — a player favor or insult, an emissary mission, a marriage, a new clan leader inheriting the old leader's grudge rows; only the game's own relation actions fire it, direct relation writes do not.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero whose relation moved (the game reroutes some changes to clan leaders or relatives)

fields.name: other
fields.description: the other hero of the effective pair

fields.name: change
fields.description: the relation points gained or lost

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's ChangeRelationDetail: Default or Emissary

fields.name: actor
fields.description: the hero the change was really aimed at; differs from `hero` when the game rerouted it

fields.name: target
fields.description: the other hero of the original pair

triggers.name: clanTierIncreased
triggers.description: A clan reached a higher tier — the player clan growing is the moment for pride or companion-slot banter.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan that just gained a tier

triggers.name: renownGained
triggers.description: A clan earned renown — `hero` is the hero whose deed brought it (usually the clan leader), `amount` what was gained; the clan is the one to react.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero whose deed gained the renown, usually the clan leader

fields.name: amount
fields.description: the renown gained

triggers.name: clanCreated
triggers.description: A new clan formed — `isCompanion` true means a companion raised to a lord just got a clan of their own; false covers rebel factions, kingdoms struck from within and excommunicated clans.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the new clan; read its leader and kingdom live

fields.name: isCompanion
fields.description: true = a promoted companion's clan; false = rebels, breakaways or excommunicated lords

triggers.name: clanChangedKingdom
triggers.description: A clan joined or left a kingdom — the player clan going mercenary or vassal, joining as a rebel faction or being absorbed by force all fire it; `detail` says exactly which move it was.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan that changed kingdom

fields.name: oldKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom left; empty when a kingdom is founded

fields.name: newKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom joined; empty when leaving without joining one

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's ChangeKingdomActionDetail: JoinAsMercenary, JoinKingdom, JoinKingdomByDefection, LeaveKingdom, LeaveWithRebellion, LeaveAsMercenary, LeaveByClanDestruction, CreateKingdom, LeaveByKingdomDestruction

triggers.name: clanDefected
triggers.description: A clan defected from one kingdom to another, dragging its parties and fiefs along — the narrower `clanChangedKingdom`; `newKingdom` is empty when it only left.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the defecting clan

fields.name: oldKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom it left

fields.name: newKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom it joined; empty if it just left

triggers.name: kingdomDecisionProposed
triggers.description: A kingdom's council began a vote on a decision — war, peace, exile and the like; the vote only starts here and the decision may still be cancelled, so treat it as news of the plan, not the result.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom whose council is voting

fields.name: playerInvolved
fields.description: true when the player is the proposer or sponsor of this vote

triggers.name: kingdomDecisionCancelled
triggers.description: A kingdom council vote was cancelled before or during — a participant died, the proposer left the kingdom, or a queued plan went stale; it will never conclude.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that dropped the decision

fields.name: playerInvolved
fields.description: true when the player was proposer or sponsor

triggers.name: kingdomDecisionConcluded
triggers.description: A kingdom council finished voting and its outcome is already in force — a decided war has been declared by the time this fires.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that decided

fields.name: playerInvolved
fields.description: true when the player was proposer, sponsor or a supporter in the vote

triggers.name: warDeclared
triggers.description: A war started between any two kingdoms or clans — including the player clan going hostile on its own; `attacker` and `defender` can be a kingdom or a clan, so test both against the player's clan and kingdom.

fields.name: attacker
fields.description: the faction that declared — a kingdom or a clan

fields.name: defender
fields.description: the faction war was declared on

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's DeclareWarDetail: how the war was started

triggers.name: peaceMade
triggers.description: Two warring factions made peace — a full kingdom war or a single clan's private feud; `detail` is `ByKingdomDecision` when a council vote ended it.

fields.name: firstFaction
fields.description: one side of the peace — a kingdom or a clan

fields.name: secondFaction
fields.description: the other side

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's MakePeaceDetail: Default or ByKingdomDecision

triggers.name: rulingClanChanged
triggers.description: A kingdom got a new ruling clan — an elected new ruler or a clan that seized power; the event only carries the old clan, so the payload reads the new ruler from the kingdom itself.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom with a new ruler

fields.name: oldRuler
fields.description: the clan that loses the crown

fields.name: newRuler
fields.description: the clan taking over, read live from the kingdom

triggers.name: kingdomDestroyed
triggers.description: A kingdom was destroyed and is about to be gone — its clans have already left it and read their new kingdoms live; comment on the end of a realm.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom being destroyed; read its last state now

triggers.name: romanticStateChanged
triggers.description: The romance between two heroes moved a step — courting, betrothal, marriage or a broken affair; in vanilla one of the two is the player.

fields.name: firstHero
fields.description: one hero of the pair; the order is not fixed, match either field

fields.name: secondHero
fields.description: the other hero of the pair

fields.name: level
fields.description: the game's Romance.RomanceLevelEnum: the romance step reached

triggers.name: heroesAboutToMarry
triggers.description: Two heroes are about to marry — the wedding action has begun but relations, households and clan moves are not applied yet; a companion is marryable only while single, so react before their status changes. The argument order may be swapped.

fields.name: firstHero
fields.description: one of the two heroes about to wed

fields.name: secondHero
fields.description: the other one

triggers.name: childEducationCompleted
triggers.description: A child hero finished an education stage — it fires at every stage of a childhood, not only the last, and `age` is the child's age at that moment.

fields.name: child
fields.description: the child who finished the stage

fields.name: age
fields.description: the child's age at the moment it fires

triggers.name: heroCameOfAge
triggers.description: A young hero came of age — a child's last stage ended and the adult world opens up.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who came of age

triggers.name: heroGrewOutOfInfancy
triggers.description: An infant hero grew out of infancy into childhood.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the child who grew out of infancy

triggers.name: heroBecameTeenager
triggers.description: A child hero became a teenager — the game may reroll their personality traits right at this moment.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the child who became a teenager

triggers.name: kingdomCreated
triggers.description: A new kingdom was founded somewhere in the world — a clan raised its banner; the player clan founding its own realm is the special case, and the outcome (ruling clan, its clans) is already set when this fires.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the new kingdom

triggers.name: tradeAgreementSigned
triggers.description: Two kingdoms signed a trade agreement with each other — kingdom news bark.

fields.name: firstKingdom
fields.description: one kingdom of the pair

fields.name: secondKingdom
fields.description: the other kingdom of the pair

triggers.name: allianceStarted
triggers.description: Two kingdoms became allies — the receiving kingdom has already accepted, and wars against their enemies follow right after.

fields.name: proposerKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that proposed the alliance

fields.name: receiverKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that accepted it

triggers.name: allianceEnded
triggers.description: The alliance between two kingdoms ended — it expired, the two allies went to war with each other, or one of the kingdoms was destroyed.

fields.name: firstKingdom
fields.description: one kingdom of the pair

fields.name: secondKingdom
fields.description: the other kingdom of the pair

triggers.name: callToWarStarted
triggers.description: One kingdom asked its ally to join a war against `targetKingdom` — the agreement is made but the war is not declared yet; when `calledKingdom` is the player's realm it is being dragged in.

fields.name: callingKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom asking its ally to join the war

fields.name: calledKingdom
fields.description: the ally being asked

fields.name: targetKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom the war will be declared on

triggers.name: callToWarEnded
triggers.description: A call-to-war agreement ended — usually straight after the war was declared, later by expiry, by peace, or when the alliance behind it ended.

fields.name: callingKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that had asked

fields.name: calledKingdom
fields.description: the ally that had been asked

fields.name: targetKingdom
fields.description: the kingdom the call to war was against

triggers.name: tributeEarned
triggers.description: A clan received gold tribute from a faction it is at war with — fires for every clan in the daily income pass, so gate on the player clan for a purse bark.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan that got the gold

fields.name: payer
fields.description: the clan or kingdom that paid the tribute

triggers.name: settlementOwnerChanged
triggers.description: A settlement changed hands — taken by siege, or handed over by barter, gift, a king's decision, rebellion, or the old owner's clan being destroyed or leaving its faction.

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the settlement that changed owner

fields.name: openToClaim
fields.description: true when the fortification is now open to claim — the game sets it for changes by siege, clan destruction or the old clan leaving its faction

fields.name: newOwner
fields.description: the hero of the clan that now owns it; empty when the fief went unassigned

fields.name: oldOwner
fields.description: the hero of the clan that lost it

fields.name: capturer
fields.description: the hero who took it by force; empty for peaceful transfers

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's ChangeOwnerOfSettlementDetail: Default, BySiege, ByBarter, ByLeaveFaction, ByKingDecision, ByGift, ByRebellion, ByClanDestruction

triggers.name: governorChanged
triggers.description: A town's governor changed — appointed, given up or replaced; on a removal `newGovernor` is empty, and an appointment is followed immediately by `heroGotBusy` with reason BecomeGovernor.

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the town or castle whose governor changed

fields.name: oldGovernor
fields.description: the governor before; empty on a first appointment

fields.name: newGovernor
fields.description: the new governor; empty when the governor was only removed

triggers.name: serviceOfferCancelled
triggers.description: A kingdom's offer to take the player's clan into mercenary or vassal service disappeared before the player decided — it expired or died from war, captivity or a changed allegiance; clicking Decline fires nothing.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.description: the kingdom that withdrew the offer

triggers.name: mercenaryServiceStarted
triggers.description: A clan went into mercenary service under a kingdom — for the player clan, right after accepting a hire offer; the new kingdom is readable live from the clan.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan that entered mercenary service

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's StartMercenaryServiceActionDetail — only ApplyByDefault in 1.4.8

triggers.name: mercenaryServiceEnded
triggers.description: A clan's mercenary service ended — it left the kingdom or became a full vassal; for the player clan the hired-sword arc is over.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan that left mercenary service

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's EndMercenaryServiceActionDetail: ApplyByDefault, ApplyByLeavingKingdom, ApplyByBecomingVassal

triggers.name: marriageOfferCancelled
triggers.description: A marriage offer to the player's kin was withdrawn — refused, expired, the clans made war, or one of the two was captured or killed; the offer banner vanishes when the game removes it.

fields.name: suitor
fields.description: the hero who had offered marriage

fields.name: maiden
fields.description: the hero who had been offered marriage

triggers.name: childConceived
triggers.description: A hero conceived a child — fires for every couple in the world, so gate on the player clan; `childBorn` follows roughly nine in-game months later.

fields.name: mother
fields.description: the mother of the unborn child

triggers.name: childBorn
triggers.description: A hero gave birth — the in-game birth of newborn children, the player's own family and companions included; the mother can be killed in childbirth right afterwards.

fields.name: mother
fields.description: the hero who gave birth

fields.name: stillbornCount
fields.description: how many of the litter were stillborn; usually 0

triggers.name: heirSelectionRequested
triggers.description: The player character just died and the game is asking which clan member takes over — the heir is not chosen yet; the candidate list is not exposed, so pair this with `heirSelected`.

triggers.name: heirSelected
triggers.description: The new heir of the player clan was chosen after a death — the player character switches right afterwards.

fields.name: heir
fields.description: the hero picked as the new heir

triggers.name: playerCharacterAboutToChange
triggers.description: The hero the player controls is about to change — fires before the old hero hands over and while they can still be read.

fields.name: oldPlayer
fields.description: the hero played until now

fields.name: newPlayer
fields.description: the hero played from now on

triggers.name: playerCharacterChanged
triggers.description: The player now controls a different hero — `heirSelected` and `clanLeaderChanged` came before; greetings for the new protagonist belong here.

fields.name: oldPlayer
fields.description: the hero played until now

fields.name: newPlayer
fields.description: the hero played from now on

fields.name: party
fields.description: the party the new player hero commands

fields.name: mainPartyChanged
fields.description: whether the main party itself changed hands

triggers.name: clanLeaderChanged
triggers.description: A clan got a new leader — succession after a death, the player-chosen heir, or a new clan lord; `newLeader` is already the leader when this fires.

fields.name: oldLeader
fields.description: the leader before the change; empty on a brand-new clan

fields.name: newLeader
fields.description: the new clan leader

triggers.name: clanDestroyed
triggers.description: A clan was destroyed — its parties, heroes and fiefs are about to be wiped; when the player's clan is destroyed the campaign is effectively over.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan being destroyed; fully readable while this fires

triggers.name: heroChangedClan
triggers.description: A lord-type hero joined or left a clan — compare `oldClan` and `newClan` for the direction; companions use `companionAdded` / `companionRemoved` instead.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who moved

fields.name: oldClan
fields.description: the clan the hero left

fields.name: newClan
fields.description: the clan the hero joined, read live from the hero

triggers.name: clanInfluenceChanged
triggers.description: A clan's influence moved — fires for every clan and every trickle, so gate on the player clan and put a `where` threshold on `change`.

fields.name: clan
fields.description: the clan whose influence moved

fields.name: change
fields.description: influence gained (positive) or lost (negative)

triggers.name: companionRemoved
triggers.description: A companion left the player clan — dismissed, killed, finished by a quest, or turned into a lord; the hero is already off the roster when this fires, so say the goodbye lines here.

fields.name: companion
fields.description: the companion who left

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's RemoveCompanionDetail: Fire, Death, AfterQuest, ByTurningToLord

triggers.name: heroGotBusy
triggers.description: A hero took up a task or role — becoming a governor, emissary, caravan or alley leader, being handed an issue, or starting to travel; the Traveling value fires very often, so filter on `reason`.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who became busy

fields.name: reason
fields.description: the game's HeroGetsBusyReasons: BecomeGovernor, BecomeEmissary, BecomeCaravanLeader, BecomeAlleyLeader, SolvesIssue, Traveling

triggers.name: heroSharedFood
triggers.description: A better-fed hero gave rations to a starving hero of the same army and gained influence for it — gratitude or indignation lines when the player's army is involved.

fields.name: supporter
fields.description: the hero who gave the food

fields.name: supported
fields.description: the hungry hero who got the food

fields.name: influence
fields.description: the influence the giver earned

triggers.name: heroTeleportRequested
triggers.description: A hero is about to be teleported on the campaign map — it fires before the move and can still be refused by the game; the typical case is a companion re-placed after being garrisoned or released.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who will be teleported

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the settlement teleported to; empty when the target is a party

fields.name: party
fields.description: the party teleported to; empty when the target is a settlement

fields.name: detail
fields.description: the game's TeleportationDetail — immediate or delayed, to a settlement or a party (as governor / party leader)

triggers.name: questLogEntryAdded
triggers.description: A quest wrote a new journal entry the player just received — it fires for every journal line of a quest, not only at acceptance or completion.

fields.name: questGiver
fields.description: the hero the quest came from — the player or one of their clan

triggers.name: issueLogEntryAdded
triggers.description: A campaign issue wrote a new journal entry the player just received — issue-arc progress between the issue's own created/resolved beats.

fields.name: issueOwner
fields.description: the hero the issue belongs to; usually the player

triggers.name: barterAccepted
triggers.description: A barter offer was accepted and the exchange is already applied — heroes, prisoners, items, gold or a fief changed hands; it also fires for lord-to-lord offers, so gate on the player side.

fields.name: offerer
fields.description: the hero who made the offer

fields.name: other
fields.description: the hero who accepted it

triggers.name: barterCancelled
triggers.description: A barter offer was refused and closed — nothing changed hands; the relation effect of the refusal shows in the relation triggers.

fields.name: offerer
fields.description: the hero who had made the offer

fields.name: other
fields.description: the hero who refused it

triggers.name: portraitOpened
triggers.description: The player opened a character portrait pop-up in a settlement or army menu; the campaign is already paused while it is open — idle flavor bark about the inspected hero.

fields.name: character
fields.description: the hero whose portrait was opened

triggers.name: boardGameFinished
triggers.description: A board game the player played ended in a win, loss or draw, before the relation and XP consequences are applied; a game the player canceled never fires it.

fields.name: opponent
fields.description: the opponent lord; empty when the opponent agent was not a hero

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: the game's BoardGameState: Win, Loss or Draw

triggers.name: tradeRumorHeard
triggers.description: The player asked a caravan captain for trade rumors and a batch of market gossip was heard — the rumor list itself is not in the payload.

triggers.name: inventoryExchanged
triggers.description: The player closed a trade, loot or gift screen and all the items have already changed parties; the counterparty gold is settled right after.

fields.name: isTrading
fields.description: true when the screen was a trade; false for looting, gifting or donating

triggers.name: itemsDiscarded
triggers.description: The player discarded items from the party inventory (loot mode, or with no other party present); the items are already gone and the payload does not say which ones.

triggers.name: tradeProfitMade
triggers.description: The vanilla trade skill counted the expected resale profit of the trade the player just closed, before the gold for it is settled.

fields.name: profit
fields.description: the estimated resale profit of this trade, in gold

triggers.name: caravanTradeCompleted
triggers.description: A caravan finished one daily buy/sell round in a town: its goods, gold and rosters are already updated; it fires for every caravan in the world, so gate on the player's own.

fields.name: caravan
fields.description: the caravan party that traded

fields.name: town
fields.description: the town it bought from or sold to

triggers.name: assetIncomeEarned
triggers.description: The player's clan was paid for one of its assets in the daily income pass: fief taxes, a tribute share, a caravan's profit or a workshop's profit.

fields.name: incomeType
fields.description: what the money came from: Taxes | TributesEarned | Caravan | Workshop

fields.name: amount
fields.description: the gold just booked; a tribute site can report a negative amount (the player paid)

triggers.name: workshopOwnerChanged
triggers.description: A workshop changed hands and the price was paid: the player bought or sold one, an heir inherited it, or the old owner died, went bankrupt or lost the town in war.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: the hero who owns it now; player-side means the clan just gained it

fields.name: previousOwner
fields.description: the hero who owned it until now; player-side means the clan sold or lost it

triggers.name: workshopTypeChanged
triggers.description: The production line of a workshop was switched and the conversion cost was paid; the payload does not say what it produces now.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: the hero who owns the workshop

triggers.name: itemProduced
triggers.description: A village or a workshop turned goods out into a settlement's store; it fires for every village and workshop in the world each day, so gate on the player's own fiefs.

fields.name: item
fields.description: the item that was produced

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the village or town whose store received it

fields.name: amount
fields.description: how many of the item were produced

triggers.name: itemConsumed
triggers.description: A workshop consumed its inputs from the town warehouse or bought them on the town market; it fires for every workshop in the world, so gate on the player's own.

fields.name: item
fields.description: the item that was consumed

fields.name: settlement
fields.description: the town whose store lost it

fields.name: amount
fields.description: how many of the item were consumed

triggers.name: itemCrafted
triggers.description: A weapon the player designed was built at a town forge and is already registered; its tier and category are on the item field, the design itself is not in the payload.

fields.name: item
fields.description: the newly crafted weapon

fields.name: isCraftingOrder
fields.description: true when it was built to fill a crafting order; then it is not added to the party inventory

triggers.name: craftingPartUnlocked
triggers.description: The player unlocked a new weapon-smithing part with smithing XP; the part itself is not in the payload.

triggers.name: itemSmelted
triggers.description: A hero at the smithing screen melted down a piece of equipment; the materials and the XP are already granted, the stamina cost comes after.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who smelted it — the hero selected in the crafting screen, not always the player

fields.name: item
fields.description: the item that was melted down

triggers.name: itemsRefined
triggers.description: Raw materials were refined into other goods and added to the party inventory, and the XP was granted; the input/output formula is not in the payload.

fields.name: hero
fields.description: the hero who refined — the hero selected in the crafting screen

triggers.name: craftingOrderCompleted
triggers.description: A weapon-smithing order was completed: its gold reward, quality bonus and perk relation effects are already applied and the order is gone from the town.

fields.name: town
fields.description: the town whose forge ran the order

fields.name: item
fields.description: the item delivered for the order

fields.name: completer
fields.description: the hero who finished it; the player when no crafting hero was chosen

triggers.name: questStarted
triggers.description: A quest the player took started and is now ongoing in the quest log; 1.4.8 keeps one global quest list, so every quest is the player's.

fields.name: questGiver
fields.description: the hero the quest came from — a lord who offered it, or a clan member

triggers.name: questCompleted
triggers.description: A quest the player had ended — succeeded, timed out, failed, was betrayed or cancelled — and its outcome hook has run.

fields.name: questGiver
fields.description: the hero the quest came from

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: the game's QuestCompleteDetails: Success, Timeout, Fail, FailWithBetrayal or Cancel

triggers.name: issueCreated
triggers.description: A new campaign issue appeared for a hero — an ongoing problem with a quest or a troop-sending solution attached; it fires across the world, so gate on the player's side.

fields.name: issueOwner
fields.description: the hero the issue belongs to; usually the player

triggers.name: issueUpdated
triggers.description: A campaign issue the player is dealing with moved one step forward: its quest started, troops were sent, or it ended in success, failure, betrayal, timeout or an AI lord's solution.

fields.name: issueOwner
fields.description: the hero the issue belongs to; usually the player

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: the game's IssueUpdateDetails step, e.g. PlayerStartedIssueQuestClassicSolution, IssueFinishedWithSuccess, IssueTimedOut

fields.name: solver
fields.description: the hero credited at this step; empty unless the player had tried before or a quest was started

triggers.name: incidentResolved
triggers.description: The player chose an option in a map incident pop-up and every consequence of that choice (gold, party morale, relations) has already run.

triggers.name: persuasionProgressed
triggers.description: The player used one option in a persuasion conversation and its result was rolled, rerolled by perks and applied; neither the option nor its result is in the payload.
